The asyncHandler Wrapper →

Why Express Needs Help with Async Errors

The one consequence of async/await that the next slide's wrapper exists entirely to work around.

Every controller function so far has been declared async, and ticket.service.js's functions are too, even without a database yet — recall from the async/await topic earlier this lesson that a rejected Promise inside an async function behaves like a thrown exception, catchable with try/catch. There's one consequence of that worth isolating on its own, because the next slide's code exists entirely because of it.

Express's routing does not await your handler. It calls getTicketById(req, res) and moves on immediately, because Express itself predates async/await being part of the language and was never rewritten to expect it:

// What Express effectively does with a route handler — it never awaits it:
router.get('/:id', ticketController.getTicketById);
// → later, roughly: ticketController.getTicketById(req, res); // not awaited

If getTicketById's returned Promise later rejects and nothing is watching it, the error vanishes into an "unhandled promise rejection" — no response is ever sent, and the request just hangs, with nothing telling the client, or you, why.

That gap — async functions reject instead of throwing, but Express never awaits them to notice — is exactly what the next slide's wrapper closes.
